shipped.kurz: The old decretals: Exiit qui seminat (1279) and Exivi de paradiso (1312)
shipped.warum: What the dispute was about, from Friedberg's Corpus iuris canonici, Latin with a working translation, in excerpts: Nicholas III declares renunciation of ownership 'not only individually but also in common' the way of Christ, explains Christ's purse as condescension to the weak, and distinguishes property, possession, usufruct, the right of using and the 'simple use of fact'; the Roman Church takes the ownership; no one may gloss it. Clement V at Vienne hears the Spirituals' list of the Community's excesses and rules on granaries and 'poor use'.

shipped.kurz: The pope's dossier: the decretals of John XXII
shipped.warum: Five decretals on 'the meaning of words', from Friedberg's Corpus iuris canonici, Latin with a working translation: obedience above poverty (1317); the question opened (1322); the Roman Church renounces its 'verbal, bare and enigmatic' ownership of the friars' goods, since no one can use an egg without owning it (1322); the assertion that Christ had nothing 'nor even in common' declared heretical (1323); the friars' 'key of knowledge' called a doctrine of the father of lies (1324).

shipped.kurz: The Book of Sentences: four Beguins handed to the secular arm (1322)
shipped.warum: Bernard Gui's general sermon at Toulouse, 12 September 1322, from the register of the inquisition printed by Limborch (1692), Latin read from the page with a working translation: Guillaume Ruffi, who asked how the Beguins burned at Narbonne had died; Pierre Dominici, who took off his crosses, called John XXII a heretic for allowing the friars granaries, and kept a litany of about seventy condemned; Pierre Hospitalis, for whom the pope had ceased to be pope; Pierre Guiraud, who would not swear to name his companions; and the sentences 'short of death', which meant death.

shipped.kurz: The order's chronicle: Perugia, the appeal, the flight (1322–1329)
shipped.warum: Nicholas Glassberger's chronicle, from the Analecta Franciscana (1887), Latin with a working translation: the letter of the general chapter of Perugia (4 June 1322) that Christ and the apostles had nothing 'individually and in common', signed by Michael of Cesena and his masters; Michael before the pope 'not as reverently as he ought'; Bonagratia's appeal and his year in a dark prison; the galley, the flight by night, the deposition at Bologna, the appeal nailed to the doors of Pisa, and the chapter of Paris that declared the pope 'had defined well'.

The general's own account, in the notarial instrument he had drawn up in secret in the Franciscan convent of Avignon, from Baluze-Mansi (1762), Latin read from the page with a working translation: summoned, sick, received 'peacefully and kindly'; then on 9 April called 'a supporter of heretics' for the Perugia letter; 'if it were heretical, Pope Nicholas would have been a heretic'; a pope who condemns Exiit condemns himself; the appeal made 'from a fear that can fall on a steadfast man'.

shipped.kurz: Dante, Paradiso XI: Francis and Lady Poverty
shipped.warum: The whole canto, in Moore's Oxford text (1904) and Longfellow's translation (1867): Thomas Aquinas tells the life of Francis as a marriage to Poverty, widowed eleven hundred years since she 'climbed the cross with Christ', and ends with the decline of his own Dominican order. Written in the years of the first phase of the dispute, before the pope's question of 1322.

planned.warum: Louis the Bavarian's appeal against the pope, with its long passage on the poverty of Christ written by Franciscans: the dispute becomes imperial politics.
planned.quelle: MGH, Constitutiones V (1909–13). Rights to be checked.

planned.warum: The answer to Ad conditorem and Quia vir reprobus, point by point, from exile in Munich: use, right, ownership, and what an act is.
planned.quelle: Goldast, Monarchia S. Romani Imperii II (Frankfurt 1614). Excerpts.

planned.warum: The inquisitor's own description of the Beguins in his Practica: what they believe about poverty, Olivi and the pope, and how to question them.
planned.quelle: Bernard Gui, Practica inquisitionis heretice pravitatis, ed. C. Douais (Paris 1886).
